# New Qutrit Codes from Pure and Bordered Multidimensional Circulant Construction Note: This material is based upon work supported by the National Science Foundation under Grant DMS-2243991.

## Abstract

We use multidimensional circulant approach to construct new qutrit stabilizer $\llbracket\ell,0,d\rrbracket$ codes with parameters $(\ell,d)\in\{(51,16),(52,16),(54,17),(55,17),(57,17)\}$ through symplectic self-dual additive codes over ${\mathbb{F}}_{9}$ . In addition to these five new codes, we use bordered construction to derive two more qutrit codes with parameters $(\ell,d)\in\{(53,16),(56,17)\}$ that improve upon previously best known parameters.

#### Keywords:

## 1 Introduction

In this work we study qutrit stabilizer codes from multidimensional circulant (MDC) graphs, and bordered MDC graphs. MDC graphs are a generalization of the well known circulant graphs to multiple coordinates and was first introduced by Leighton in [5]. Recently, in [8], Seneviratne et al., used MDC graphs to obtain new zero dimensional qubit stabilizer codes that improved previously best known parameters. Additive self-dual codes over ${\mathbb{F}}_{9}$ have gotten much less attention compared to their counterparts over ${\mathbb{F}}_{4}$ .

Let ${\mathbb{F}}_{9}=\{0,1,\omega,\ldots,\omega^{7}\}$ , where $\omega^{2}=\omega+1$ and $\omega^{4}=-1$ . An additive code $C$ ol length $n$ over ${\mathbb{F}}_{9}$ is a ${\mathbb{F}}_{3}$ -linear subgroup of ${\mathbb{F}}_{9}^{n}$ . The weight of a vector ${\bf v}\in{\mathbb{F}}_{9}^{n}$ is the number of nonzero entries of ${\bf v}$ . The least nonzero weight of all codewords in $C$ is called the minimum distance of $C$ . If $C$ is an additive code of length $n$ over ${\mathbb{F}}_{9}$ with minimum distance $d$ and size $3^{k}$ , then $C$ is denoted by $(n,3^{k},d)_{9}$ . The conjugation of an element $x\in{\mathbb{F}}_{9}$ is given by $\overline{x}=x^{3}$ . The Hermitian trace inner product of two vectors ${\bf x,y}\in{\mathbb{F}}_{9}^{n}$ is defined by $\left\langle{\bf x,y}\right\rangle=\omega^{2}({\bf x}\cdot\overline{{\bf y}}-\overline{{\bf x}}\cdot{\bf y})$ . The dual code $C^{\perp}$ , with respect to the Hermitian trace inner product is defined by $C^{\perp}=\{{\bf u}\in{\mathbb{F}}_{9}^{n}\mid\left\langle{\bf c,u}\right\rangle={\bf 0}\;\mbox{for all}\;{\bf c}\in C\}$ . An additive code is self-dual if $C=C^{\perp}$ . A self-dual code has parameters $(n,3^{n})$ . A code which is self-dual with respect to the Hermitian inner product $\langle\bf{x},{\bf y}\rangle={\bf x}\cdot\overline{{\bf}y}$ over ${\mathbb{F}}_{9}$ , is also self-dual with respect to the trace Hermitian inner product [2].

## 2 Qutrit codes from multidimensional circulant graphs

#### Definition 1.

[5] A MDC graph $G({\bf N},S)$ has the vertex set $V(G)=\{(a_{1},\ldots,a_{k}):a_{1}\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{n_{1}},\ldots,a_{k}\in{\mathbb{Z}}_{n_{k}}\}$ and two vertices ${\bf a}=(a_{1},,\cdots,a_{k})$ and ${\bf b}=(b_{1},,\cdots,b_{k})$ are adjacent if and only if $(a_{1}-b_{1}\ (mod\ n_{1})),\cdots,a_{k}-b_{k}\ (mod\ n_{k}))\in S$ , where ${\bf N}=(n_{1},n_{2},\ldots,n_{k})$ , $S\subset{\mathbb{Z}}_{n_{1}}\times Z_{n_{2}}\times\cdots\times{\mathbb{Z}}_{n_{k}}$ , with $S=-S$ and ${\bf 0}\notin S$ .

#### Example 1.

*Figure 1: The $3$ -cube graph as a MDC graph*

Figure $1$ represents the hypercube graph $Q_{3}$ as a MDC graph with parameters $N=(2,4)$ and $S=\{(0,1),(0,3),(1,0)\})$ . The upper layer contains the vertices in $V_{0}$ as $1,\ldots,4$ and the lower layer presents the vertices in $V_{1}$ as $5,\ldots,8$ .

An adjacency matrix $\Gamma=\Gamma(G)$ of a MDC graph $G$ is a nested block circulant matrix as described in [8].

#### Theorem 1.

The adjacency matrix $\Gamma(G)$ of a MDC graph $G({\bf N},S)$ has nested block circulant form

$$ \Gamma(G)=\begin{pmatrix}A_{1,1}&A_{1,2}&\ldots&A_{1,{l-1}}&A_{1,l}\\
A_{1,l}&A_{1,1}&\ldots&A_{1,{l-2}}&A_{1,{l-1}}\\
\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\
A_{1,3}&A_{1,4}&\ldots&A_{1,1}&A_{1,2}\\
A_{1,2}&A_{1,3}&\ldots&A_{1,l}&A_{1,1}\end{pmatrix}, $$

where $\mathbf{N}=(n_{1},n_{2},\ldots,n_{k})$ , with $n_{1}\leq n_{2}\leq\ldots\leq n_{k}$ and each block $A_{1,j}$ is a $N_{1}\times N_{1}$ submatrix of $\Gamma(G)$ for $1\leq j\leq n_{1}$ , and $N_{1}=\frac{(n_{1}n_{2}\cdot n_{3}\cdots n_{k})}{n_{1}}$ , $N_{2}=\frac{N_{1}}{n_{2}}$ , $N_{3}=\frac{N_{2}}{n_{3}}$ , $\ldots$ , $N_{k}=\frac{N_{k-1}}{n_{k}}$ .

The following result stated in [2] ensures that the additive codes obtained from $3$ -weighted graphs are self-dual with respect the Hermitian trace inner product. A graph $G=(V,E,W)$ is an $m$ -weighted graph if $W$ is a set of weights in ${\mathbb{F}}_{m}$ associated to each edge of $G$ with the vertex set $V$ and $E\subseteq V\times V$ is the edge set of $G$ .

#### Theorem 2.

[2] Let $\Gamma$ be the adjacency matrix of a $3$ -weighted graph, $I$ the identity matrix, and a primitive element $\omega\in{\mathbb{F}}_{9}$ . The additive code $C_{G}$ with the generator $\Gamma_{G}=\Gamma+\omega\cdot I$ is in standard from and is self-dual with respect to the Hermitian trace inner product.

When the length $n$ ranges from $1$ to $40$ we ran an exhaustive search to generate every possible self-dual additive code over ${\mathbb{F}}_{3}$ that could be generated with MDC graphs. We present a table that provide a comparative study between qutrit codes generated with MDC and optimal qutrit codes listed in Grassl’s Table [3].

### 2.1 New qutrit codes

We present five new qutrit codes $Q_{51},Q_{52},Q_{54},Q_{55}$ , and $Q_{57}$ obtained from MDC graphs by using a randomized search method. Minimum distance of the codes $Q_{51},Q_{52},Q_{54},Q_{55}$ , and $Q_{57}$ were computed using the Magma computer algebra system [1]. It took $8$ hours, $9$ hours, $12$ days, $11$ days, and $16$ days to verify the minimum distances of these codes.

#### Proposition 3.

A new self-dual additive code $C_{51}$ with parameters $(51,3^{51},16)_{9}$ and the resulting $\llbracket 51,0,16\rrbracket_{3}$ qutrit code $Q_{51}$ is derived from the the MDC graph $G_{51}:=G((3,17),S)$ with

$$ \begin{split}&S:=\{(1,1),(1,2),(0,4),(1,10),(1,15),(0,7),(1,4),(2,13),(0,9),(0,1),(0,16),(2,2),(0,8),\\
&(1,11),(0,3),(0,11),(2,15),(1,16),(2,11),(1,12),(2,1),(1,9),(0,5),(0,12),(0,14),(2,8),\\
&(2,5),(0,13),(2,6),(0,10),(1,6),(1,13),(2,4),(0,6),(2,16),(2,7)\}\end{split} $$

$Q_{51}$ improves the minimum distance of the $\llbracket 51,0,15\rrbracket_{3}$ code in the Grassl’s qutrit code database [3] by $1$ .

#### Proposition 4.

A new qutrit code $Q_{52}$ with parameters $\llbracket 52,0,16\rrbracket_{3}$ that improves the minimum distance of the best known code by $1$ , is generated via an additive self-dual code $C_{52}$ obtained from the MDC graph $G_{52}:=G((4,13),S)$ , where

$$ \begin{split}&S:=\{(3,1),(3,4),(0,10),(1,9),(3,6),(3,0),(1,12),(0,2),(1,3),(2,5),(0,11),(3,9),(1,0),(2,8),(3,8),\\
&(1,7),(0,3),(1,4),(1,5),(3,10)\}\end{split} $$

#### Proposition 5.

The MDC graph $G_{54}:=G((3,18),S)$ , where

$$ \begin{split}&S:=\{(1,1),(1,2),(1,14),(1,5),(1,15),(0,7),(2,13),(2,3),(0,1),(0,8),(0,11),(2,15),(2,11),(1,12),\\
&(1,7),(2,1),(0,5),(2,17),(1,9),(0,12),(1,17),(2,5),(0,17),(0,13),(2,9),(2,6),(1,3),(0,10),(2,12),\\
&(1,6),(1,13),(2,4),(2,16),(0,6)\}\end{split} $$

generates a new qutrit code $Q_{54}$ with parameters $\llbracket 54,0,17\rrbracket_{3}$ and improves upon the previous best known minimum distance given in [3] by $1$ .

#### Proposition 6.

The MDC graph $G_{55}:=G((5,11),S)$ , where

$$ \begin{split}&S:=\{(1,1),(1,2),(3,3),(1,10),(1,5),(1,4),(3,6),(0,9),(4,3),(0,1),(4,4),(3,2),(3,10),(0,2),\\
&(1,7),(4,1),(2,1),(1,9),(3,0),(4,8),(4,10),(2,8),(2,5),(4,9),(2,9),(1,3),(0,10),(3,4),(2,10),\\
&(4,6),(2,0),(4,2),(3,1),(1,8),(4,7),(2,7)\}\end{split} $$

generates the code $C_{55}$ , with parameters $(55,3^{55},17)$ and the corresponding qutrit code $Q_{55}$ has parameters $\llbracket 55,0,17\rrbracket_{3}$ .

#### Proposition 7.

A new qutrit code $Q_{57}$ with parameters $\llbracket 57,0,17\rrbracket_{3}$ is generated via an additive self-dual code from the MDC graph $G_{57}:=G((3,19),S)$ , where

$$ \begin{split}&S:=\{(0,7),(0,2),(2,17),(2,0),(0,16),(1,2),(0,14),(2,8),(1,4),(0,10),(1,18),(0,17),(0,9),\\
&(1,11),(1,15),(2,4),(0,12),(0,5),(2,5),(1,8),(0,6),(2,13),(1,0),(2,15),(1,6),(2,18),(0,13),\\
&(2,1),(0,11),(0,1),(2,11),(1,1),(1,14),(0,3),(1,7),(2,12),(0,18),(0,8)\}\end{split} $$

## 3 Bordered multidimensional construction

When studying self-dual codes, the bordered construction is a well-known technique employed by coding theorists to extend the length of a code. The bordered construction had been successfully applied in [4, 6] to classify additive self-dual codes over ${\mathbb{F}}_{4}$ , and in [7], the bordered construction was used to obtain two new qubit codes with parameters $\llbracket 81,0,20\rrbracket_{2}$ and $\llbracket 94,0,22\rrbracket_{2}$ from metacirculant graphs. In this section, we will study additive self-dual codes obtained from bordered adjacency matrices of MDC graphs.

Let $A:=A(G)$ be the multidimensional circulant adjacency matrix of a MDC graph $G({\bf N},S)$ . A bordered MDC matrix

$$ \overline{A}=\begin{bmatrix}0&1&\cdots 1\\
1&&\\
\vdots&A&\\
1&&\end{bmatrix} $$

is the adjacency matrix of the graph $\overline{G}$ , which is the graph obtained by adding an extra vertex $v_{\infty}$ to the graph $G$ and connecting $v_{\infty}$ to all other existing vertices.

We used a randomized search on bordered MDC graphs to obtain two new qutrit codes with parameters $\llbracket 53,0,16\rrbracket_{3}$ and $\llbracket 56,0,17\rrbracket_{3}$ . The minimum distance of these codes were calculated using Magma [1].

#### Proposition 8.

The bordered MDC graph $\overline{G}_{52}$ with $G_{52}=G((2,26),S)$ , where

$$ \begin{split}&S=\{(1,1),(1,2),(1,25),(0,4),(1,10),(1,5),(1,15),(0,9),(0,23),(1,21),(1,11),(0,3),(1,24),\\
&(0,11),(1,16),(0,2),(0,15),(0,12),(0,14),(0,17),(0,24),(0,20),(1,3),(1,0),(1,23),(0,22),(0,6)\}\end{split} $$

generates a new $(53,3^{53},16)_{9}$ additive self-code $C_{53}$ . The corresponding $\llbracket 53,0,16\rrbracket_{3}$ code $Q_{53}$ improves the minimum distance of the best known code given in Table [3] by 1.

#### Proposition 9.

A new additive self-dual code $C_{56}$ with parameters $(56,3^{56},17)$ and a corresponding new qutrit code $\llbracket 56,0,17\rrbracket_{3}$ , $Q_{56}$ is generated by the bordered MDC graph $\overline{G}_{56}$ , with $G_{56}:=G((5,11),S)$ , where

$$ \begin{split}&S:=\{(0,4),(3,3),(3,7),(3,6),(1,4),(0,7),(2,3),(4,3),(0,8),(2,2),(0,3),(3,5),(1,9),(4,8),(3,9),(2,8),\\
&(2,5),(4,5),(3,8),(2,6),(1,3),(3,4),(1,6),(2,4),(4,2),(1,8),(4,7),(2,7)\}.\end{split} $$

$Q_{56}$ improves the minimum distance of the best known qutrit code given in Table [3] by $1$ .

## 4 Concluding Remarks

We have shown that MDC graphs can be effectively used to construct optimal ternary quantum error-correcting codes. MDC construction enable us to generate longer length codes efficiently than the circulant construction.
